title: Threaded rod with a trapezoidal helical thread
purpose: Generate a closed threaded rod whose radius follows a trapezoidal thread profile along a helix, with flat crest and root. Use it for bolts, screws, jar necks and lead screws.

entry_points.name: thread_profile
entry_points.summary: Height of the thread in [0, 1] at ``phase`` (fraction of the pitch): root flat, rising flank, crest flat, falling flank, each flank (1 - crest - root) / 2 of the pitch.

entry_points.name: screw_thread
entry_points.signature: screw_thread(major_radius=0.2, minor_radius=0.16, pitch=0.1, length=0.8, crest=0.15, root=0.25, segments=32, samples_per_pitch=8)
entry_points.summary: A closed threaded rod centred at the origin along Y: (rows + 1) * segments vertices, rows * segments quads and two polygon caps, where rows = ceil(length / pitch * samples_per_pitch). The radius at angle theta and height y is minor + (major - minor) * profile(y / pitch - theta / 2 pi): a right-hand thread.

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.summary: Command line: write the threaded rod as .gltf or .obj and print a JSON summary.

parameters.name: minor_radius
parameters.meaning: Radius at the thread root; below major_radius.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.meaning: Axial distance between neighbouring crests (one turn for a single start).

parameters.name: length
parameters.meaning: Length of the rod along Y.

parameters.name: crest
parameters.meaning: Fraction of the pitch that is flat at the crest.

parameters.name: root
parameters.meaning: Fraction of the pitch that is flat at the root; crest + root < 1.

outputs.content: one welded mesh with POSITION and NORMAL, indexed triangles
the same rod as Wavefront OBJ

limits: A single right-hand start; the ends are cut flat through the thread without a chamfer. The flanks are sampled on a fixed grid, so the crest and root corners are only as sharp as the axial sampling. Dimensions are free numbers, not tied to a thread standard.
technique_references: Helical radius function r(theta, y) = minor + depth * profile(y / pitch - theta / 2 pi)
